Penumbra's Factions and Moon Aspects

The Iron Moon 
Faction: The Iron Hands (Warrior Archetype)
Pragmatic, Blunt, Uncompromising - Force
Pragmatically-minded folk who believe the threat of force is necessary and honest. All guards and most sellswords are members of this faction.
Quote: “Might makes right”
Physical-damage weapons and armour
Skills are largely martial, based on hitting harder and being damaged less.
Verbs: Hit, Survive

The Pallid Moon 
Faction: The Bone Herders (Necromancer Archetype)
Haughty, Mystical, Nihilistic - Spirit
Dedicated to the mysteries of life and death, and the manipulation of both. The Bone Herders are unsettling folk, dissatisfied with their immortality and somewhat obsessed with the Final Deaths of the pre-Gloom period. They intentionally starve themselves to remain close to ‘The Veil’.
Quote: “Death is the path to truth”
Magic-damage weapons and magic-resistant armour
Skills are based on the manipulation of bones and spirits
Verbs: Curse, Cast, Call

The Dusk Moon 
Faction: The Dusk Cartographers (Ranger Archetype)
Curious, Cheerful, Observant - Perception
Enthusiastic explorers of the overworld who sell maps whose very existence is capable of temporarily stabilising areas of Gloom. If you journey out into the world, you’ll likely find yourself in contact with these folk more than any other, usually in the company of a few Iron Hands.
Quote: “Reveal that which is hidden”
Long-range weapons
Skills based on sight, positioning, mapping and Gloom manipulation
Verbs: Perceive, Target, Move

The Shaded Moon
Faction: The Lantern Bearers (Monk Archetype)
Hardy, Loyal, Quiet - Resistance
Miners and stonemasons who initially fashioned and now maintain the Underways. For these folks, light is holy, to be treasured as much as water or food. What they lack in finesse they make up for with sheer force of will.
Quote: “Light purifies all”
Lights, charms, amulets, cloaks and other resistance-based objects
Skills are based on status changes, and the manipulation of sight, light and darkness
Verbs: Endure, Purify, Silence

The Turning Moon 
Faction: The Toymakers (Crafter Archetype)
Playful, Enthusiastic, Mercurial - Intellect
While they may seem childlike and occasionally lacking in tact, the Toymakers are able to craft almost anything from anything, producing everything from complex gadgets to mechanical companions.
Quote: “Creation is art, art is life” 
Gadgets of all forms, including wands, orbs and even Golems
Skills based on crafting, creation and maintenance of various useful gadgets
Verbs: Create, Improve, Play

notes.title: Version 1.0.1. Build 948
notes.notes:
Yes, it's still alive. 

This is a bug-fix for an old->new game save which - in more professional hands, or even professional flippers - would be labelled a 'Hotfix'. However, I am British, and while it is, indeed, a 'fix' it is in no way 'hot'. 

It doesn't leer at me across the restaurant table wearing mere whispers of diaphanous chiffon, eyes kohl rimmed pits of mystery and excitement. Nor does it whisper strange, flirtatious words into my ear in a crowded lift while standing just a little too close for decency. 

No. This is the sort of fix that shuffles into the room dressed in a baggy sweater, eyes glued to the floor, mumbling something barely audible about 'save games' and 'incompatibility issues', only to make a hasty exit, leaving you wondering silently at the subtle loveliness of the face you glimpsed beneath the torrents of unkempt hair that your fingers now long to comb through.

Yes. Definitely more the latter.

notes.title: Build 932 - Boring Patch
notes.notes:
No, you can't dig or drill. It's not that kind of boring. It's the other kind. It's the 'Slideshow... dull... losing... consciousness...' kind of dull. You don't believe me? For f- 

Look.

- [DONE] Creatures now properly save their Shield status
- [DONE] One certain creature now retains their Shield status between save/load states
- [DONE] Fixed the Buy panel which had some display errors when wrapping from bottom to top position
- [DONE] Change to Harlequin description so that it's not utter nonsense (no idea what happened there!)
- [DONE] Properties now cause faction opinion changes when they change, not continuously
- [DONE] New 'factions' console command that reveals all faction values
- [DONE] Harrodius' Amulet now has a shorter description that doesn't flood the box

See? I wasn't lying. It's boring. Banal. Dull. Tedious. It's like that Friday morning geography lesson with Mr Hendriks who only had one vocal tone which he insisted on piping through his peculiarly hairy nose. It's that book all your friends insist was really good when all it did was present a series of lists of 1980s pop culture. It's that 'new banger' of a song with lyrics that are the equivalent of "Aw, yeah, baby yeah, I want you, let's dance on the dance floor (as opposed to, presumably 'in the larder'), yeah."

It's thoroughly uninteresting. The only compelling aspect of this update is this message which contains a singular and rather shocking deliberate misspelling. You were warned.

- Fluttermind































































Yes, I lied about that spelling mistake, too. I was desperate.

notes.title: Build 925 - PIT-y-less update
notes.notes:
ALRIGHT! I GET IT. PEOPLE HATE TRAPSDOORS! (Yes, I know they're not Pit traps, but I had a very bad 'joke' I wanted to use and I was going to use it, regardless. You are not the boss of me.) 
Jeez. 

Um... what can I do about that?
Uh, I could just get rid of them completely? No. That would be giving in to the howling throng. I'm never doing that. No.
Hmm.

What about, I make Perception ridiculously powerful as a tool for spotting traps?

And what if I make discovered trapdoors so ridiculously visible you could see them from space (if there wasn't a vast dust-cloud and a selection of creepy moons blocking the view)?

Oh! I could reduce the amount of trapdoors rather than removing them completely?

Or, I could do none of these and post a completely empty patch! AHAHAHAHAHA.
No. That would be too cruel and... stupid. Yes. Stupid. Dumber than a box full of dead frogs... or whatever the common parlance is for stupid boxes of things. Hammers? I don't know. Where was I?

Oh, yes. I could also do ALL OF THE ABOVE instead. Ahahahaha! That'll teach them! YES! AHAHAHAHAHA!

notes.title: Build 912 - The 'Stop Borking Your Dungeons Between Versions' Update
notes.notes:
Hey folks,
Thanks as ever for your patience. This update is a little strange.
Not many people know the difficulty of maintaining the validity of save games over a long period.
Moonring has been in development for a long time, and - as a result - the save formats, and the various underlying pieces of code to ensure compatibility between versions has grown longer and more complicated. This fix marks my removing a section of code that was nuking dungeon data between saves. This was, at one point, necessary. It hasn't been for a long time and I thought I'd cleaned it up.

Well, I sort of cleaned it up. It was more like cleaning a bullet wound and leaving the bullet in there. To become infected. And icky. As a result, each new build has been 'Working Fine on My Machine (TM)', but various reports have described ghostly stairwells that don't actually go up and other creepy occurrences. 

This is now gone, and I think the saves should be more robust without that old code festering in there.

Also, Stunning Roar now hits players a lot harder thanks-k-bye!

notes.title: Major update! Build 859
notes.notes:
Hey folks,

It's been a while, but I've been kind of busy with this release. 
Uh... I've... totally removed all the old dungeons. Bye! 

Wait, you want more information than that? Oh boy. Okay...

All of the old Relic Dungeons have now been replaced with the new dungeon code based on 'Herringbone Wang Tiles'. It's a super-fast technique that allows me to generate dungeons super quickly.

So. You're going to find the startup is now close to instant. All 'building world' messages are gone. 

If you're curious, or are one of those folks who likes to talk about 'Lazy devs' (a breed I've never met, and I put in the same bucket as 'unicorns', 'bigfoot' and 'a valid use of NFTs') I've also done these other things:

notes.title: Build 761 - Major Changes to UI and Input
notes.notes:
Hey folks,

Thanks for your patience! I know it's been a while since the last update.
Over the last month, I've basically ripped apart a ton of the input mechanisms, parts of the display and various other things. The result should beL:

- Full Steam Deck compatibility (yes, including the text size!)
- A new approach to the conversation system
- Fewer bugs
- Faster everything... I hope.

I've not forgotten you all, nor your support over the last few months. Lemme know if there are issues with this build, and if not, I'm going to push it to the main branch! 

Fixes to:
-Overhaul of Luck/Crit system
-Overhaul of Durability->Sell price
-Massive overhaul to UI allowing re-adability on small screens
-Massive overhaul to UI allowing joystick control of entire game
-Dungeon level 'joined tiles' are sometimes not joined if you exit and re-enter
-Remove ability to have 2 player ships
-Enter heart site at 397 318 to anchor your reset. Sail away and die while zoomed on your ship. Ship is removed!
-Charged double at inns, but that doesn't stop you staying if you have insufficient funds
-Puppet causing crash when used on Pushers
-Igniting oil only caused temporary flames
-Oil not creating central patch on throw
-Durabiliy not taken into account in sell-price
-Dying in an inconvenient place can leave you stranded without a ship

Have fun,

- Dene

notes.title: Version 744 - The Big One
notes.notes:
Hey folks,

My birthday is in two days, so - much like my anniversary - I thought it a really good time to make a major release public. I am a master at this stuff.

Yes, this build has been a long time coming. In the last few months I've been working really hard to try and make this game the best I can given my limitations. So many bugs have been fixed. So many systems have been improved. There's a lot more to come, and the game still isn't perfect, but I hope you find it way more stable, faster, and lower in WTF quotient.

Major Changes:
- Major crashes fixed (particularly the Pit trap, Tower of Veils and - please God - the Jest)
- A mini-keyboard for all you Steam Deck types. At some point I'll add a default config which makes sense, too... when I know how!
- Totally revamped save system. It's way more forgiving, so my apologies to the hardcore folks. That said...
- Someone asked for... I can't believe I'm saying this... a... Permadeath mode. Sigh. Well. You only have yourselves to blame.

And so much more.

In addition to this, my favourite label - Heimat Der Katastrophe - are releasing a full Moonring OST on Wednesday 6th of December, first on digital, then on cassette on the 8th! I shall be receiving ZERO from this, but it's something I always wanted to do and it's my birthday, damnit. 

Anyway, please enjoy. And thanks for sticking around on the ride. This isn't the last you'll be hearing of Moonring, not by a long way.

- Dene

P.S. T-shirts available at RobaRoba.
No more news on cloth maps just yet. Booo.
